units.label: page 1

Mars Rover Mission
Your task is to plan a complete mission for a rover on Mars. The rover must travel through the map, complete 
all required tasks, use charging stations when necessary, manage its limited data storage, transmit collected 
data to Ground Control, and finally reach the destination.
You do not need to find the most optimal or shortest possible route. Your route only needs to be valid and 
complete all necessary tasks. However, a shorter route will usually require fewer instructions to transmit.
Rover instructions:
F – Forward: Move one square forward in the direction the rover is facing. F costs 1 energy unit.
L – Turn left: Rotate 90 degrees to the left. The rover stays on the same square.
R – Turn right: Rotate 90 degrees to the right. The rover stays on the same square.
U – U-turn: Rotate 180 degrees. The rover stays on the same square.
Ph – Photo: Take a photograph on a Photo square. Each Photo square contains an arrow. The rover must be 
standing on the Photo square and facing in the direction of the arrow when it uses Ph.
Pi – Pick: Collect a sample on a Sample square. The rover must be standing on the Sample square when it 
uses Pi.
Ch – Charge: Recharge the rover on a Charging Station square. After Ch, the battery is restored to 10 energy 
units.
T – Transmit: Send all collected scientific data to Ground Control and clear the rover's data storage. T can be 
used from any square and does not consume energy.
Energy:
The rover starts with 10 energy units.
Only F consumes energy. Every F costs 1 energy unit.
The rover may not move forward when its energy is 0.
To continue, the rover must be standing on a Charging Station square and use Ch.
L, R, U, Ph, Pi, Ch and T do not consume energy.
Data storage:
The rover can store a maximum of 3 data items.
Each Ph and each Pi creates 1 data item.
When the storage already contains 3 data items, the rover may continue to move and turn, but it may not 
use Ph or Pi again until it uses T.
T sends all stored data to Ground Control and clears the storage back to 0 data items.
The rover may use T at any time, but unnecessary transmissions make the instruction sequence longer.
All collected data must be transmitted before the rover reaches the destination.
Special squares:
Photo square: The rover must visit the square and use Ph while facing the direction shown by the arrow on 
that square.
Sample square: The rover must visit the square and use Pi to collect the sample.
Charging Station: The rover may use Ch here to restore its battery to 10 energy units.
Obstacle / inaccessible terrain: The rover cannot enter this square.
